Title: Who can win Super Bowl LX? Identifying contenders outside of top tier that can hoist Lombardi Trophy - CBSSports.com

Summary: 
As of Week 5 of the 2025 NFL season, the league is perceived as wide open despite early favorites like the Buffalo Bills, Philadelphia Eagles, Detroit Lions, Kansas City Chiefs, and Green Bay Packers suffering setbacks. With the top five betting favorites eliminated, the analysis focuses on second-tier teams with odds between +1500 and +4000 to win Super Bowl LX. The Baltimore Ravens remain at +1500 due to Lamar Jackson’s presence, but their 1-4 start and injury-plagued defense—especially the loss of Pro Bowl defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike—undermine their chances. The Jacksonville Jaguars lead the NFL in takeaways (13) and rank highly in rushing (144.0 ypg, 5.0 ypc), yet struggle with quarterback play, as Trevor Lawrence has a 58.3% completion rate and 75.1 passer rating. The Indianapolis Colts have impressive wins over weak teams but lack a proven path against elite competition, and their schedule ease may not translate in the playoffs. San Francisco 49ers, despite injuries, are 4-1 and benefit from Kyle Shanahan’s coaching and a strong core; their recovery timeline could elevate them. The Los Angeles Chargers have declined after a strong start, with Justin Herbert throwing three interceptions in two games, raising concerns about his performance under pressure. The Seattle Seahawks, despite a 38-point loss to the Bucs, show promise with Sam Darnold’s 73.1% completion rate and 114.8 passer rating, and a strong defense that could peak in the postseason. Denver Broncos, at 3-2, are buoyed by a strong defense and a favorable remaining schedule, while second-year QB Bo Nix’s development under Sean Payton could unlock their potential. Washington Commanders benefit from Jayden Daniels’ return, who led a road win despite limited health, and have shown NFC Championship-level capability. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 4-1 and atop the NFC South, have a 'comeback' identity, with Baker Mayfield’s four fourth-quarter comebacks tied for the most in NFL history through five games. However, the Los Angeles Rams are deemed the most capable of winning the Super Bowl due to their talent and resilience, despite self-inflicted losses—such as Kyren Williams’ fumble in a close game and a blown 26-7 lead—suggesting they can improve under Sean McVay’s guidance.

Title: CBS Sports predicts 49ers win Super Bowl, Brock Purdy named NFL MVP

Summary: 
CBS Sports writer John Breech projects the San Francisco 49ers to finish the 2025 season with a 13‑4 record, earning the top NFC seed. He also predicts the Arizona Cardinals at 10‑7, the Los Angeles Rams third and the Seattle Seahawks fourth in the NFC West. Across the conference, Breech names the Philadelphia Eagles the No. 2 seed with a 12‑5 record, the Green Bay Packers and Tampa Bay Buccaneers winning their divisions, and the Washington Commanders and Detroit Lions securing the final Wild Card spots. In a bold move, Breech declares Brock Purdy the NFL MVP, citing his 2023 season of 4,280 yards and 31 touchdowns and the 49ers’ favorable 2025 schedule, the league’s easiest by strength of schedule. He predicts the 49ers will defeat the Eagles 30‑27 in the NFC Championship and then beat the Baltimore Ravens 27‑24 in Super Bowl LX at Levi’s Stadium, capturing the team’s first Lombardi Trophy since 1994. Breech notes the 49ers’ injury history and past Super Bowl shortcomings but remains optimistic, highlighting defensive coordinator Robert Saleh’s return and the presence of elite playmakers Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle. He concludes, 'Before 2020, no team had ever won a Super Bowl in their home stadium, but with this game, the 49ers will become the third team in five years, joining the 2020 Buccaneers and the 2021 Rams.'
